title: Move or copy: what a drop should do
summary: You know drag and drop. Learn when a drop should move or copy, and how to protect people when a drop can't be taken back.
objective: Choose move or copy for any drop from its source and destination, and add the right safeguard when a drop can't be undone.

source.title: Drag and drop, Human Interface Guidelines (Apple)

hook.prompt: Someone drags a photo from the Photos app into an email they're writing in Mail. After the drop, where should the photo be?

options.text: Only in the email
options.feedback: That's how dragging a real object works, but here it would quietly take the photo out of their library.

options.text: In both Photos and the email
Wherever the person picks in a dialog
options.feedback: A dialog on every drop slows down something people do constantly. There's a sensible default.

hook.explanation: Between apps, a drop always copies. Why, and when a drop moves instead, comes next.

bricks.title: Same container moves; anywhere else copies
bricks.body: After a drop, **moved** content exists only in the destination; **copied** content exists in both places. The default comes from the containers. Within the **same container**, such as one text view or document, a drop moves. Into a **different container** it copies, and between apps it always copies. With a physical keyboard, check **Option at drop time**: held, a same-container drop copies; released before the drop, it moves.

visual.alt: Four drags and their results: within one document, a move; into another document, a copy; into Mail, always a copy; within one document with Option held, a copy.
visual.html:
DragResult

Image from one document into anotherCopy
A file from your app into MailCopy, always

bricks.template: Mia drags a paragraph lower in the same document, holding Option the whole time: a [[a]]. Then she drags another paragraph and lets go of Option just before dropping: a [[b]].

mistakes.feedback: Without Option this would be a move, but she's holding it at drop time, which forces a copy.
Option is checked when the drop happens, not when the drag starts. She released it, so the same-container default applies.

bricks.explanation: Option is read at drop time. Held at the drop: a copy. Released before it: the same-container default, a move.

bricks.prompt: Your Mac writing app shows two text views side by side in a split view. Someone drags a sentence from one view into the other. What should happen to the original sentence?

options.text: It stays where it was
It disappears, since both views belong to the same app
options.feedback: The default follows containers, not apps. Two text views are two containers, so the drop copies.

options.text: It becomes a link to the new copy
options.feedback: A drop either moves or copies; neither default turns the original into something else.

bricks.hint: Count the containers, not the apps.
bricks.explanation: Each text view is its own container, so the drop copies and the sentence stays in the source view.

bricks.prompt: Holding Option, someone drags an image from one document into a different document. What's the result?

options.text: A copy
A move
options.feedback: Option forces a copy within one container. It never turns a copy into a move, and this drop crosses containers.

options.text: Nothing: Option cancels the drag
options.feedback: Option changes what a same-container drop does, not whether the drop happens.

bricks.hint: What would this drop do without Option?
bricks.explanation: Different containers already copy. Option only matters when a same-container drop would otherwise move.

bricks.prompt: A teammate's spec lists drop behavior for your Mac notes app. Tap the row that breaks the defaults.

visual.html:
Drag a note to a new spot in the same listMove
Drag a checklist item into a different noteCopy
Drag a note from our app into MailMove
Option held at the drop, within one noteCopy

bricks.hint: Check which rows cross from one app into another.
bricks.explanation: Dragging into Mail crosses apps, and drops between apps always copy, so the note must stay in the notes app.

bricks.title: When a drop can't be taken back
bricks.body: People sometimes drop content in the wrong place, so **prefer undo**. When a drop can't be undone, protect people another way: **confirm before** it completes, as Finder does before a file goes into a write-only folder people can't open, or **offer a way to reverse it after**, as Photos lets people cancel sharing a photo dropped into a shared stream. Before changing the move or copy defaults, choose what's least likely to cause frustration or data loss.

visual.alt: A confirmation dialog asking whether to put Report.pdf in Drop Box, warning that the file can't be seen or removed afterwards, with Cancel and Put in Folder buttons.
visual.html:
Put “Report.pdf” in “Drop Box”?

You can't open this folder, so you won't be able to see or remove the file after you drop it.

bricks.situation: In your expenses app, dragging a receipt onto the **Approved** column sends it to payroll at once. Payroll can't recall it.

options.text: Ask for confirmation before the drop completes
options.outcome: Someone who grabbed the wrong receipt sees the question and cancels. Nothing reaches payroll by accident.

options.text: Let it drop, then show a “Sent to payroll” notice
options.outcome: People know what happened, but after a wrong drop they find out too late to stop it.

options.text: Support Edit > Undo for the drop
options.outcome: Undo moves the card back, but payroll already has the receipt. The app now shows something that isn't true.

bricks.hint: Can anything in the app take this drop back once it's happened?
bricks.explanation: Payroll can't recall the receipt, so undo can't really reverse it. Protection has to come before the drop, while the mistake can still be stopped.

bricks.prompt: Dropping a file into a team's shared folder syncs it to everyone at once, and undo can't unsync it. Which notice after the drop is better?

visual.alt: A notice reading Shared Brief.pdf with the Design team, with a Stop sharing button.
visual.html:
Shared “Brief.pdf”

Everyone in Design can see it now.

visual.alt: A notice reading Shared Brief.pdf with the Design team, with only an OK button.
visual.html:
Shared “Brief.pdf”

Everyone in Design can see it now.

options.feedback: It tells people what happened, but leaves no way back if they dropped the file into the wrong folder.

bricks.explanation: Undo can't take this drop back, so a way to reverse its result, stopping the share, still lets people recover from a wrong drop.

bricks.prompt: A teammate wants image drags between documents to *move* instead of copy, so documents don't fill up with duplicates. What's the strongest case against it?

options.text: People expect a copy, so images would vanish from the source document
Moves can't be undone
options.feedback: A move can be undone like any drop. The problem is that people won't expect the image to leave its source.

options.text: Option would stop working
options.feedback: Option would still force a copy within one container. The issue is the cross-document default people rely on.

options.text: Moving content between documents isn't possible
options.feedback: It's possible. The defaults are about what people expect, not what the system can do.

bricks.hint: Picture the source document right after the drop.
bricks.explanation: A changed default should favour what people expect and what's least likely to lose data. A surprise move out of the source risks both.

challenge.prompt: In your photo library app, someone drags 20 photos onto **Family**, a shared album in the sidebar. Adding photos sends them to relatives at once, and that can't be undone. Which design fits?

options.text: Copy the photos into the album, and offer a way to cancel sharing after the drop
Move the photos into the album, and support undo
options.feedback: The library and the album are different containers, so the photos should stay in the library. And undo can't recall photos relatives already have.

options.text: Copy the photos into the album, and rely on Edit > Undo
options.feedback: The copy is right, but undo can't pull back photos that were already sent. People need a way to reverse the sharing itself.

options.text: Move the photos into the album, and ask for confirmation first
options.feedback: The safeguard works, but the default doesn't: the library and the album are different containers, so moving would empty the library of those photos.

challenge.hint: Answer two things separately: same container or not, and can undo take this back?
challenge.explanation: Library and album are different containers, so it's a copy. Sharing can't be undone, so people need a way to reverse it, like cancelling the share.

takeaways: Default to a move within one container and a copy across containers; drops between apps always copy.
Check Option at the moment of the drop: held, a same-container drop becomes a copy.
Prefer undo; when a drop can't be undone, confirm before it or offer a way to reverse it after.
Before changing a default, pick the behavior least likely to surprise people or lose data.
